title: Longest Continuous Increasing Subsequence
prompt: Given an unsorted array of integers `nums`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray that is strictly increasing. A subarray is contiguous, unlike a general subsequence, so `nums[i] < nums[i+1]` must hold for every consecutive pair within it.

examples.explanation: The longest continuous increasing subarray is [1,3,5], with length 3. Even though [1,3,5,7] would be longer as a subsequence, 5 and 7 are not adjacent.
No two adjacent elements are strictly increasing, so the answer is 1.

hints: This is a single left-to-right scan, not a search over all subarrays.
Maintain a window that grows as long as each new element continues the increasing run, and restarts the moment it doesn't.
Track the window's start index (or just its current length) and reset it to the current position whenever nums[i] <= nums[i-1].

solution.approach: Walk through the array while maintaining the length of the current increasing run. Whenever the current element is greater than the previous one, the run extends by one; otherwise a new run starts at the current element. This is a sliding window whose left boundary resets to the current index every time the increasing property breaks. Track the maximum run length seen.
